title: Underwriting and the duty to take reasonable care
product: Insurance Contracts Act 1984 and Corporations Act 2001 s1019B
version: Rule guide FY2026-27 v1.0 — current at 23 Nov 2026 (Insurance Contracts Act compilation from 8 Oct 2026)
summary: What a client must do when applying for life insurance, how an insurer can respond to a misrepresentation, the protection for genetic information that started on 8 Oct 2026, the cooling-off period, and how Caldova handles underwriting outcomes. Uma's Underwriting Agent explains the duty in plain English before any health question; Claims uses the remedies when it checks an older policy.
limits: AI agents never answer health questions for a client, never suggest what to leave out, never ask for genetic test results, and never accept a loading, an exclusion or a decline on a client's behalf. Cooling-off ends once a claim has been made. The 3-year limit in s29(3) doesn't apply to fraud.
evidenceRequired: Application and disclosure answered by the client, after the duty to take reasonable care was explained
Medical evidence the insurer requires for the age and sum insured (e.g. blood profile, medical examination)
Financial evidence for income protection and business protection
Client's signed acceptance of any loading or exclusion
sources: Insurance Contracts Act 1984 s20A, s20B (including s20B(5A) from 8 Oct 2026), s29, s30 and s33H — https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A02944/latest/text
